title: RDF/SPARQL verification procedure
summary: Apply data and query verification to RDF graphs and SPARQL in the target engine.

sections.label: Inputs
sections.text: TTL change, ontology/shapes version, graph fixtures, SPARQL queries, expected outputs, and target environment.

sections.label: Procedure
items: Exercise positive, negative, scope, missing-data, and temporal scenarios.
Check API-visible semantics and named-graph selection.
For an Amazon Neptune deployment, use its measured execution plans when investigating performance. For another RDF engine, use that engine's supported diagnostics and measured workload.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Report engine, dataset, query, expected result, actual result, and limitations. Structural validity does not establish source truth.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Apply RDF specific checks during Tests and review and repeat the affected query and structural cases when verifying a repair. Existing Neptune diagnostic and SHACL links remain scoped technology references. No live endpoint, engine compatibility or passing RDF verification was established by this gap review.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: The report identifies engine, dataset, ontology and shapes revisions, query text and expected versus observed results.
The structural result is retained with positive, negative, missing data, named graph and temporal cases selected for the change.
Performance findings cite measured target engine diagnostics and workload, while source truth and unrun cases remain separate.

catalog.applicability: Use this RDF and SPARQL procedure when the workflow uses RDF data and SPARQL. Supply the actual engine, graph scope, vocabulary, fixtures and structural rules, and use Neptune execution plans only for a Neptune deployment.
catalog.limits: SQL and property graph procedures need their own checks. Neptune diagnostics apply only to Neptune. Reading this procedure does not run a query, install an integration or verify source truth.
